inputs.note_net_debt: Negative net_debt means net cash position (cash exceeds debt by $41.3B). Sourced from FY2025 10-K: $132B total liquidity vs $90.7B term debt.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is unreliable for Apple due to $85-100B/yr buybacks creating volatile book equity (equity declined from $65B in FY2020 to $57B in FY2022, then rebounded to $74B in FY2025 as buyback pace and profits fluctuated). EPS 5yr CAGR of 17.9% is elevated because it captures buyback-driven per-share amplification rather than pure operational growth. FCF 5yr CAGR of 6.1% is the most reliable growth anchor for DCF, consistent with revenue 5yr CAGR of 8.7% when adjusted for one-time items. Note: FY2022-FY2024 revenue was essentially flat (~$391-394B range), compressing 3yr CAGRs; H1 FY2026 reacceleration to +16% YoY reflects the iPhone 17 / Apple Intelligence cycle.

base.description: Apple Intelligence upgrade cycle drives above-historical-trend growth in FY2026-FY2027, decelerating as the cycle matures. Services continues compounding at double-digit rates. Buybacks persist at $90-100B/yr. No catastrophic regulatory outcome on Google TAC.
base.wacc_rationale: Apple's WACC of 8.5% reflects: (1) risk-free rate ~4.3% (10yr UST), (2) equity risk premium ~5%, (3) beta ~0.85-0.90 (low volatility, defensive Services revenue growing), (4) very low leverage (net cash), (5) modest regulatory risk premium. CAPM implied equity cost ~8.5-9%. With negligible debt cost weighting, WACC approximately equals cost of equity at 8.5%.
base.note: FCF growth rates applied to FY2025 FCF base of $98,767M. Rates of 8%, 7%, 6%, 5%, 4% reflect strong near-term momentum (H1 FY2026 +16% revenue YoY) decelerating to mature large-cap growth by year 5.

bull.description: AI supercycle triggers multi-year iPhone upgrade wave. Services accelerates to 30%+ of revenue mix by FY2030 driving blended margin expansion. India demand + manufacturing diversification reduces cost and risk. Google TAC revenue preserved or replaced. CEO Ternus maintains execution discipline.
bull.note: Bull WACC 8.0% reflects higher confidence in earnings quality and lower perceived regulatory risk. Terminal growth 3.0% justified by Services installed base monetization engine continuing to compound.

bear.description: Google TAC payment ($12.5-20B) prohibited by antitrust remedies, removing near-pure-profit revenue. EU DMA forces App Store commission cuts. iPhone upgrade cycle disappoints as Siri/AI fails to differentiate. Tariff escalation compresses Products margins. China share losses continue.
bear.note: Bear WACC 9.0% reflects elevated regulatory uncertainty, potential $12.5B+ annual revenue loss from Google TAC, and broader compression of App Store economics. FCF growth near-flat as margin compression offsets any revenue growth.

base.note: Base IV $136.61 represents fair value on a 5yr FCF-only DCF. The $159 gap to current price reflects the market pricing in (a) higher long-term FCF growth beyond year 5, (b) accelerating buyback EPS amplification, (c) terminal year margin expansion from Services mix, and (d) growth option value from Apple Intelligence / India / health tech. The DCF as modeled is intentionally conservative on forward growth.

entry_price.description: Entry price required to achieve 15% CAGR over 5 years, discounting Terminal Value per share at 15%^5. Entry Price = (Terminal Value / Shares) / (1.15)^5

probability_weighted.weight_rationale: 40% base / 30% bull / 30% bear: Apple's regulatory headwinds (Google TAC, DMA, Epic contempt, DOJ suit) are numerous and credible, warranting above-average bear probability. The bull case (AI supercycle) has early empirical support from H1 FY2026 data but depends on continued execution. Weights reflect balanced uncertainty around a strong-but-fairly-valued business.

sensitivity.matrix_description: Intrinsic value per share (USD). Rows = WACC, Columns = Terminal Growth Rate
sensitivity.note: Even at the most bullish WACC/TG combination (7.5% WACC, 3.5% TG), base case FCF projections yield $197/share vs current $295.63 — a 33% discount to market. This highlights that the market is either pricing in significantly higher growth rates beyond Y5, or assigning a premium multiple to Apple's Services/AI optionality not captured in a 5yr DCF horizon.

sanity_check.method: Compared implied multiples at base case IV vs 10-year historical average multiples and recent 3-year average multiples

historical_multiples.pb_ratios_note: P/B skipped per instructions — Apple's massive buybacks have created negative or near-zero book equity in recent years, making P/B analytically meaningless for this company

trip_checks.pb_skip_reason: Apple P/B is analytically useless due to buyback-driven near-zero equity

sanity_check.conclusion: NO SANITY TRIPS DETECTED. The base case IV of $136.61 implies P/E of 18.0x and EV/EBITDA of 13.5x — both below their respective 10-year historical averages (24.4x and 17.9x). The DCF is therefore internally consistent and if anything conservative relative to how the market has historically valued Apple. The gap between IV ($136.61) and current market price ($295.63) is a valuation premium the market is paying, not a DCF modeling error. The current market price of $295.63 implies P/E of 38.9x and EV/EBITDA of 29.6x — both above the 10yr average and at the high end of the recent 3yr range. The market is pricing in sustained high growth from Apple Intelligence, Services compounding, and buyback EPS amplification that a conservative 5-year FCF DCF does not fully capture.

market_price_check.qualitative_note: The current market price is not irrational given Apple's Services transformation (75%+ margin vs historical hardware-only profile), but it does embed significant optimism about AI execution, regulatory outcomes, and sustained capital return at current pace. Risk/reward at $295 appears unfavorable on a DCF basis.

key_assumptions: Base case: FCF grows 8%/7%/6%/5%/4% over 5 years from FY2025 base of $98.8B, reflecting iPhone 17 cycle and Services compounding decelerating to mature large-cap pace. WACC 8.5%, terminal growth 2.5%. Net cash of $41.3B added back. 14,726M shares (Q2 FY2026 diluted). Bull case: 12%/10%/9%/7%/6% FCF growth, WACC 8.0%, TG 3.0% — AI supercycle scenario. Bear case: 3%/2%/2%/1%/1% FCF growth, WACC 9.0%, TG 2.0% — Google TAC loss + regulatory compression + margin pressure scenario. FCF growth is applied directly to LTM FCF rather than modeling revenue-to-FCF margins separately, consistent with Apple's stable ~23-25% FCF margin over FY2021-FY2025.
wacc_rationale: Apple's WACC of 8.5% (base) / 8.0% (bull) / 9.0% (bear) is derived as follows: Risk-free rate = 4.3% (10yr US Treasury as of mid-2026). Equity risk premium = 5.0% (Damodaran US ERP). Beta = 0.85 (Apple's realized 3yr beta on monthly returns; Services revenue growing as a stabilizing force; Apple has historically been less volatile than the broader market on a trailing basis despite tech classification). CAPM: 4.3% + 0.85 * 5.0% = 8.55%. Apple's capital structure is essentially all-equity on a net basis (net cash positive), so WACC approximately equals cost of equity. The 8.5% base rate slightly rounds down CAPM to reflect the exceptional credit quality, $41B net cash buffer, and highly recurring Services revenue (now 26% of revenue at 75%+ margins). The bear case adds 50bps to reflect regulatory event risk and potential earnings uncertainty from Google TAC decision.
dcf_limitations: 5-year explicit forecast horizon may underweight Services terminal value; Services at 75%+ margins likely warrants a longer runway or a segment-specific DCF
Buyback impact on per-share value is captured implicitly via shares_outstanding reduction over time, but the model does not explicitly project declining share counts in each projection year
Apple Intelligence platform optionality, Vision Pro long-term potential, and health technology options are not explicitly valued — they are embedded in the terminal growth rate assumption
Google TAC ($12.5-20B at risk) is scenario-addressed in bear case but not probabilistically weighted within base case; actual outcomes are binary and court-dependent
FCF in FY2025 was $98.8B, below FY2022 ($111.4B) and FY2024 ($108.8B) peaks — FCF has been range-bound while the stock has doubled; this base year conservatism anchors the DCF below market valuation
